business.title: Post-retrofit building performance dataset: Energy, IEQ, HVAC operation, and occupant behavior in university apartment buildings
business.description: This paper presents a comprehensive monitored dataset from single-family attached residences that underwent deep energy retrofits, complementing a previously published pre-retrofit dataset from the same buildings. The dataset is distinct by its multi-domain scope and temporal resolution, simultaneously capturing whole-building and end-use energy consumption, indoor environmental quality, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) system operation (including thermostat setpoints and supply air temperature), window and door operation, building envelope performance, and outdoor environmental parameters at sub-hourly intervals. Data were collected from sixteen occupied apartments across two residential buildings over a continuous twelve-month period, enabling detailed analysis of performance across all seasonal conditions. This high-resolution, multi-faceted dataset uniquely documents the coupled dynamics between building envelope functions, HVAC systems operation, occupant interactions, and weather conditions in the post-retrofit state. A semantic metadata model of building systems and sensors was developed using a JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) schema. Standardized cleaning and pre-processing steps were applied to produce a research-grade dataset. Post-retrofit results reveal improved thermal stability, enhanced ventilation effectiveness with reduced CO2 concentration, and measurable energy performance improvements compared to pre-retrofit conditions. This openly available dataset provides researchers and practitioners with a unique opportunity to evaluate retrofit impacts through granular time-series analysis, study occupant-building-weather dynamics, perform comparative pre/post retrofit analysis, and develop predictive models for human-centered, energy efficient building transitions.

science.title: ACSL5 suppresses pancreatic cancer progression and gemcitabine resistance by regulating n-6 docosapentaenoic acid metabolism
science.description: Gemcitabine (GEM) resistance remains a major challenge in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) treatment. Metabolic reprogramming is a hallmark of tumors, and imbalance in lipid metabolism promotes tumor progression and drug resistance. This study aims to elucidate the mechanism of Acyl-CoA Synthetase Long Chain Family Member 5 (ACSL5) in PDAC, its impact on fatty acid metabolism, and its clinical relevance. Through RNA sequencing, targeted metabolomics, proteomics, retrospective cohort studies, and a series of in vitro and in vivo experiments, the significance of ACSL5 was systematically investigated. Our results showed that ACSL5 was downregulated in GEM-resistant cells, and its high expression predicted better survival in PDAC patients. ACSL5 overexpression suppressed proliferation, migration, invasion, and GEM resistance in PDAC cells, while its knockdown promoted these phenotypes. ACSL5 may exert its effects through the PPARδ/CPT1A signaling pathway, thereby influencing fatty acid β-oxidation. Notably, ACSL5 selectively modulated n-6 docosapentaenoic acid (DPA-n6) levels, while prospective cohort studies have shown that high plasma DPA-n6 is an independent risk factor for poor prognosis. Junction Plakoglobin (JUP) was identified as an ACSL5-binding protein and was associated with ACSL5 ubiquitination and protein stability. In summary, ACSL5 acts as a tumor suppressor in PDAC by modulating fatty acid metabolism. DPA-n6 may serve as a novel prognostic biomarker, highlighting the clinical relevance of ACSL5-associated lipid metabolism in PDAC.

science.title: Patterns of multiple long-term conditions in patients presenting with breathlessness and their associations with adverse outcomes
science.description: Patients presenting with breathlessness often have pre-existing diagnoses of multiple long-term conditions (MLTC). We investigated baseline patterns of MLTC and their associations with downstream rates of health service utilisation and risk of mortality in a cohort of patients with a first recorded code for breathlessness. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Clinical Practice Research Datalink (CPRD). Adults with a first recorded code for breathlessness were included. Patients with MLTCs (≥ 2 long-term conditions (LTC)) formed the main cohort, while those with ≤ 1 LTC served as controls. Latent class analysis (LCA) identified classes with similar MLTC patterns. Regression models compared two-year health-service utilisation and five-year mortality between MLTC classes and controls. We identified 57,163 patients with MLTCs and 44,206 controls. Thirteen classes of patients with distinct patterns of MLTCs were identified through LCA. The ‘depression-prevalent with co-occurring anxiety and hypertension’ class had the highest relative rates of primary care consultations, while the ‘hypertension-prevalent with co-occurring cerebrovascular disease’ class had the highest relative rates of unplanned hospital admissions, compared with controls. Five-year mortality risk was highest in the ‘learning disability-prevalent with co-occurring epilepsy’ class. Distinct MLTC patterns in adults presenting with breathlessness were associated with variation in healthcare use and mortality. Our results highlight opportunities for improved mechanistic understanding, risk stratification and appropriation of clinical care.

science.title: Schiaparelli impact basin on Mars, filled with deposits
science.description: The rim of the 450-kilometre-wide Schiaparelli crater impact basin stands at only approximately two kilometres high. As a rule of thumb, the ratio of crater diameter to crater depth is around 10:1, meaning that after the impact of an asteroid up to 40 kilometres in size, Schiaparelli was initially a depression around four to five kilometres deep. Volcanic deposits, lake sediments and material carried in by the wind are likely to have filled the basin over the past three to four billion years. This can be seen, among other things, in the small craters within the crater floor, which are filled with deposits almost up to their rims. The crater rim itself is already heavily eroded.
